title: Annotatio IV §.XV: Lanfranc quotes Berengar — sacrament does not cease what it was; visible sign, invisible res
pass_a_gloss: But among Writings opposed to Berengar, Lanfranc of Canterbury’s book On the Truth of the Lord’s Body in the Eucharist stands out, repeating the following words of Berengar: Through the Consecration of the altar, bread and wine become a Sacrament of Religion; they do not cease to be what they were, but that they may be changed into another and become what they were not. Again: The Sacrifice of the Church consists of two things, the visible sacrament and the invisible thing of the sacrament, i.e. the body of Christ. Again: Sacraments are Visible seals of divine things, but the invisible things themselves are honored in it.
pass_b_english: Among opposing books, Lanfranc of Canterbury On the Truth of the Lord’s Body stands out — and repeats Berengar’s own words.

By altar consecration bread and wine become a Sacrament of Religion yet do not cease what they were; the Church’s sacrifice is visible sacrament plus invisible res (Christ’s body); sacraments are visible seals — the invisible things are what is honored.
source_text: Inter opposita verò Berengario Scripta, Lanfranci Cantuariensis de Veritate Corporis Domini in Eucharistia, liber eminet, sequentia Berengarii verba repetens: Per Consecrationem altaris, panis & vinum fiunt Sacramentum Religionis, non desinunt esse quod erant, sed ut in aliud mutentur & fiant quæ non erant. Iterum: Sacrificium Ecclesiæ duobus constat, visibili sacramento & invisibili re sacramenti, i. e. corpore Christi. Rursus: Sacramenta sunt Visibilia rerum divinarum signacula, sed res ipsæ invisibiles in eo honorantur.
